questions.prompt: An adult referred for sleep testing reports severe daytime sleepiness while routinely sleeping only four to five hours because of rotating shifts. What information is most important to document before attributing the complaint to a primary hypersomnolence disorder?
options: Whether the patient prefers a morning appointment
Usual sleep schedule, sleep duration, shift pattern, and relevant medication use
Whether the patient has ever used a nasal pillow mask
The preferred EEG screen color
questions.answer: Usual sleep schedule, sleep duration, shift pattern, and relevant medication use
questions.rationale: Restricted or irregular sleep and substances can confound assessment of excessive daytime sleepiness; the clinical evaluation must account for sleep opportunity and schedules.

questions.prompt: During hookup, the eye-movement channel remains nearly flat during instructed left-right eye movements while EEG responds normally. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Assume the patient cannot enter REM sleep
Verify the EOG electrodes, connections, derivation and calibration before recording
Raise every channel's high-frequency filter to conceal the problem
Remove the EOG channels from the montage without explanation
questions.answer: Verify the EOG electrodes, connections, derivation and calibration before recording
questions.rationale: A failed channel-specific biocalibration is a setup or acquisition problem until electrode, derivation and equipment integrity are checked.

questions.prompt: A technologist is preparing standard EEG sites for a PSG. Which approach best supports reproducible placement across patients?
options: Estimate sites from the patient's hairstyle
Use measured anatomical landmarks and the prescribed electrode-placement system
Place both electrodes directly over the ears
Choose different unmeasured positions whenever a cable seems short
questions.answer: Use measured anatomical landmarks and the prescribed electrode-placement system
questions.rationale: Standardized landmark measurements support consistent electrode locations; montage and technical requirements should be checked against the current AASM manual.

questions.prompt: A 12-year-old has a PSG before a planned MSLT. The recording provides eight hours in bed but only six hours and twenty minutes of sleep. What should the technologist do?
options: Treat this as meeting the pediatric minimum sleep-time protocol
Ignore the PSG because the MSLT uses only daytime data
Flag the short sleep time and communicate with the ordering team under the laboratory's protocol before proceeding
Substitute a home pulse-oximetry result for the missing sleep
questions.answer: Flag the short sleep time and communicate with the ordering team under the laboratory's protocol before proceeding
questions.rationale: The 2024 pediatric MSLT guidance calls for an attended PSG allowing at least eight hours in bed and seven hours of sleep; insufficient sleep requires protocol review.

questions.prompt: An adult is scheduled for MSLT immediately after a split-night study in which PAP pressures were adjusted. Which response best protects test validity?
options: Proceed without noting the titration because the patient slept at least once
Recognize that an MSLT should not follow a PAP-adjustment night and contact the ordering team about rescheduling or further direction
Replace the first nap with an extra ECG lead
Use the overnight recording as the first MSLT nap
questions.answer: Recognize that an MSLT should not follow a PAP-adjustment night and contact the ordering team about rescheduling or further direction
questions.rationale: The adult AASM protocol excludes MSLT after a split-night or initial PAP titration because the preceding sleep and treatment conditions can confound interpretation.

questions.prompt: A nine-year-old child's PSG was scored using adult respiratory criteria merely because the scorer used a default adult software template. What is the best quality-review action?
options: Keep the template without checking age or the laboratory's approved scoring pathway
Check patient age and the applicable AASM pediatric versus optional adult scoring pathway, then review affected events under the authorized approach
Average the adult and pediatric results automatically
Convert all pediatric respiratory events to arousals
questions.answer: Check patient age and the applicable AASM pediatric versus optional adult scoring pathway, then review affected events under the authorized approach
questions.rationale: A nine-year-old requires pediatric respiratory scoring rules. The current AASM FAQ allows—but does not require—adult respiratory rules beginning at age 13; default software settings cannot override the selected age-appropriate rule set.

questions.prompt: A respiratory sensor failed for a substantial part of a study, then was replaced successfully. What should the technical report and handoff preserve?
options: Only a statement that all sensors were normal at the end
Timing of signal loss, corrective action, restoration and any limitation on data quality
A revised interpretation written independently by the technologist
No notation because the signal returned
questions.answer: Timing of signal loss, corrective action, restoration and any limitation on data quality
questions.rationale: The record must support subsequent scoring and interpretation by making equipment problems and periods of non-interpretable data traceable.

questions.prompt: During adult PSG review, repeated apparent oxygen dips align exactly with loss of the plethysmographic waveform during hand movement. What should the scorer do before accepting the drops as physiological evidence?
options: Confirm the pulse-oximetry signal quality and cross-check accompanying respiratory/physiological channels
Automatically count every displayed dip as a scored respiratory event
Infer sleep stage N3 from the oxygen channel
Remove all movement annotation from the record
questions.answer: Confirm the pulse-oximetry signal quality and cross-check accompanying respiratory/physiological channels
questions.rationale: Poor plethysmographic signal can create false SpO2 changes; scoring and reporting require signal validation and the applicable current AASM criteria.
